# Lummis Releases Updated Clarity Act Text

July 22, 2026

Washington, D.C.— Today, Senate Banking Digital Assets Subcommittee Chair Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) released updated text for the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633), which reflects the merged work products of the Banking and Agriculture Committees.

“This is another step in my years-long journey to ensure the U.S. leads the way on digital assets,” said Lummis. “The U.S. has always been at the forefront of financial innovation, and the coming weeks are likely the last real chance we will have for years to get this right. I want to thank Chairman Scott, Chairman Boozman, and Leader Thune for their support and leadership, and I look forward to partnering with them to ensure the U.S. leads the way in digital assets for generations to come. # White House Signs Off on CLARITY Act Ethics Deal, Reopening a Path to a Senate Vote Before Recess

Jason Jones 21 Jul 2026

Assets: BTC

Clarity Act, Crypto

The breakthrough on the bill's most stubborn provision arrives with days to spare before the August break, and it removes the single obstacle that had stalled crypto's landmark market-structure law.

For most of July, the story of the CLARITY Act was a story about one paragraph. Not the jurisdictional split between the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, not the DeFi carve-outs, not the illicit-finance provisions that critics kept circling. The whole bill hinged on an ethics clause governing conflicts of interest for senior government officials, and until this week that clause had refused to close.
